note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: In Jamaica, which body inspects a new electrical installation and certifies it before the power company will connect the supply?
options: The power company's meter reader
The municipal corporation's building inspector
The Government Electrical Regulator
The Bureau of Standards Jamaica

questions.stem: A type B breaker trips each time a pump motor starts, although the running current is well within its rating. The breaker datasheet shows types B, C and D. What is the best change?
options: A type C breaker of the same rating, as the designer approves
A type B breaker rated above the cable's current rating
The same type B breaker, with the motor started twice
Any breaker with the same frame size, whatever its type

questions.stem: A datasheet says a type C breaker trips instantly at between 5 and 10 times its rated current. In what current range does a 20 A type C breaker trip instantly?
A breaker is marked 6 kA breaking capacity. The designer's figure for the largest fault current at the board is 9 kA. What does this tell you?
options: It is suitable, because 6 kA is far above its rated current
It may fail to clear a fault; a higher kA rating is needed
It will trip faster than usual on overload
The cable on that circuit must be made smaller

questions.stem: An RCD datasheet gives its rated residual operating current (IΔn) as 30 mA. What does this tell you?
options: It trips when current leaking to earth reaches about 30 mA
It can carry a load current of up to 30 amperes safely
It trips when the load current reaches 30 mA
It limits any fault current to 30 mA

questions.stem: The label on an RCD says the test button should be pressed quarterly. How often is that?
options: Every week
Every month
Every three months
Every year

questions.stem: A motor's rating plate shows IP55, insulation class F and duty S1. Which job does it suit best?
options: Short bursts with long rests, in a dry room
Running non-stop on a pump in a dusty, damp pump house
Working under water at the bottom of a well
Running in a room where explosive vapour may be present

questions.stem: A motor's rating plate gives a full-load current of 9.6 A. How is this figure used when setting its overload relay?
options: Set it to about twice 9.6 A so it does not trip at start-up
Set it to the rating of the circuit breaker
Set it to the lowest point on the dial
Set it to 9.6 A, as the relay maker's instructions say

questions.stem: A cable rating table has columns for 'clipped direct', 'in conduit on a wall' and 'in an insulated wall'. Why are the ratings different?
options: Each method uses a different type of cable
The supply voltage is different for each method
Only clipped cable may carry its full rating
Heat escapes from the cable at a different rate

questions.stem: A cable table is based on an air temperature of 30 °C. The cable will run in a roof space in Kingston that reaches 45 °C. What must you do?
options: Apply the maker's correction factor for 45 °C
Use the table figure, since 45 °C is normal here
Add 15 A to the rating to allow for the heat
Ask the client to fit a fan in the roof space

questions.stem: An LED floodlight datasheet says: 'Input 100–240 V AC, 50 Hz, 150 W, power factor 0.9 or more.' On which of Jamaica's supplies can it be used?
options: Only on 220 V, because 110 V is too low
Only on 110 V, because 220 V is too high
On either 110 V or 220 V, as both are in range
On neither of them, unless a step-down transformer is used

questions.stem: A specification calls for IPX4 light fittings in a shower room. What does the X mean?
options: The fitting has no protection at all against water
Protection against solid objects is not stated
The fitting is sealed against all dust
The fitting was tested four times over

questions.stem: Which of these two ratings gives more protection against water: IP44 or IP66?
options: IP66
IP44
Both are the same
It depends on the voltage

questions.stem: A breaker's datasheet gives a terminal torque of 2.5 N·m, but your torque screwdriver is marked only in lbf·in. What should you do?
options: Tighten by feel, since the units do not match
Set the tool to 2.5 on its lbf·in scale, as the numbers match
Tighten as hard as you can, to be safe
Convert the value with a reliable table, then set the tool

questions.stem: During an inspection you find scorch marks around one terminal of a breaker. What is the most likely cause?
options: The breaker is the wrong colour for the board
A loose or under-tightened connection
The cable is larger than the load needs
The board cover was fitted upside down

questions.stem: What should the circuit chart (board schedule) fixed inside a distribution board door show?
options: The price paid for each breaker and the supplier's name
The order in which the circuits were wired
Each circuit, its load, its device and its cable size
The names of the electricians who wired it

questions.stem: Which drawing shows how a motor starter works, with each device drawn in its circuit in logical order rather than where it sits in the panel?
options: A layout drawing
A block diagram
A schematic diagram
An as-built floor plan

questions.stem: When you wire a control panel, which drawing tells you where each wire physically lands, terminal by terminal?
options: The connection (wiring) diagram
The block diagram
The site location plan
The single-line diagram of the supply

questions.stem: What does a single-line diagram of a building's supply mainly show?
options: Every conductor drawn separately, in its colour
The main parts of the supply and how they connect
Where each light switch and socket is, room by room
Only the earthing and bonding arrangement

questions.stem: A specification names one make of fitting, followed by the words 'or approved equal'. What does this mean?
options: Any cheaper fitting may be used
Only that exact fitting may be used
The installer decides what counts as equal, without asking
Another fitting may be used if the designer approves it

questions.stem: A specification says: 'Emergency lighting shall give light for at least 3 hours after mains failure.' What kind of requirement is this?
options: A performance requirement: it states the result needed
A material requirement: it names the product to be used
A location requirement: it shows where it goes
A staffing requirement: it says who installs it

questions.stem: A specification says: 'All final circuits shall be insulation-tested at 500 V DC before they are energised, and the results recorded.' Which is correct practice?
options: Test only the circuits that look damaged
Test with the circuits live, so that all the loads are included
Test every circuit dead, with sensitive equipment disconnected
Test at the highest voltage the tester can give

questions.stem: Which set of documents should the client receive at the handover of a new installation?
options: The final invoice and nothing else
The suppliers' price lists for the equipment
The site diary, the team's time sheets and the delivery notes
Test certificates, as-built drawings and the manuals

questions.stem: Drawing E-03 Rev C has a cloud drawn around one area, with a small triangle marked 'C' beside it. What does this show?
options: That area is not to be built
What was changed in revision C
A fire-rated zone of the building
A detail that is not drawn to scale

questions.stem: A maker issues a safety notice: a batch of RCDs may not trip. Several RCDs were fitted on your site last month. What should the team leader do?
options: Wait until the next periodic inspection
Check batch numbers, report it, replace as the notice says
Remove the test labels from the RCDs
Tell the client the RCDs passed a test once, so they are fine

questions.stem: The specification shows a solar inverter in a closed cupboard. The maker's manual says it needs 300 mm of free air on each side and must not be enclosed. What should you do?
options: Follow the specification, because the client wrote and paid for it
Fit it in the cupboard and leave the door open
Drill some air holes in the cupboard door
Raise a query, as the spec would break the maker's terms

questions.stem: Why can installing equipment against the maker's instructions cost the client money later?
options: The maker may refuse the warranty if it fails
The power company will charge a higher rate
The equipment will use more energy straight away
The inspector will charge a higher fee

questions.stem: The safety data sheet for a cable jointing resin says it causes serious eye irritation and may cause a skin allergy. Which PPE does this point to?
options: A hard hat only
Ear defenders and a dust mask
Goggles and suitable chemical-resistant gloves
A high-visibility vest and steel-toed safety boots

questions.stem: A battery room door shows a pictogram of liquid dripping onto a hand and onto a metal bar. What hazard does it warn of?
options: Flammable gas only
Radioactive material in the batteries
Hot surfaces that can burn the skin
Corrosive substances

questions.stem: A UPS manual says its vented lead-acid batteries must be kept in a ventilated room. Why?
options: So the battery labels stay dry and readable
Charging can give off hydrogen, which can explode
So the acid in the cells can dry out between charges
So the batteries can be heard when they fail

questions.stem: A motor drive's datasheet gives an operating range of 0–40 °C. It is to go in a metal kiosk in full sun in Santa Cruz, where the inside reaches 55 °C. What should you do?
options: Raise it: it needs cooling, shade or another place
Fit it as shown, because a datasheet is only a guide
Fit it, and leave the kiosk door open
Fit it, and turn the speed down on hot days

questions.stem: A datasheet gives a leakage current to earth of 3.5 mA. How many amperes is this?
An imported air-conditioner manual asks for 12 AWG copper conductors, which are about 3.3 mm². Your store has only metric sizes. Which size should you use?
options: 2.5 mm², as it is the nearest size
1.5 mm², because metric cable is better
4 mm², the next size that is not smaller
Any size, since AWG sizes have no meaning in Jamaica

questions.stem: A cable drum label reads '3C 4 mm² XLPE/SWA/PVC 600/1000 V'. What does '600/1000 V' tell you?
options: The length of cable on the drum
Its current rating in amperes
The test voltage to use on it after it is installed
Its voltage rating to earth and between conductors

questions.stem: On a cable label, what does 'XLPE' describe?
options: The steel wire armour
The insulation, cross-linked polyethylene
The colour of the outer sheath of the cable
The metal used for the conductors

questions.stem: An earthing specification says the earth electrode resistance shall not be more than 25 Ω. Which reading fails?
options: 9 Ω

questions.stem: In a maker's manual, what does a box headed 'NOTE' usually give?
options: Helpful extra information, not a hazard warning
A warning that serious injury or death is likely
The number of the standard the product meets
The prices of spare parts

questions.stem: A machine manual says: 'Isolate and lock off before opening the terminal box.' A co-worker says the motor is already stopped at its stop button. What is right?
options: The stop button is enough, as the motor is not running
Isolate, lock and tag, then prove dead with a tester checked before and after
Open the box carefully, using insulated tools
Ask someone to stand guard by the start button

questions.stem: You have waited the discharge time given in a motor drive's manual. What must you still do before touching its DC bus terminals?
options: Touch them quickly with the back of your hand
Check that the display screen has gone blank
Short them out with a screwdriver blade
Measure the DC bus voltage to prove it has discharged

questions.stem: A specification gives socket heights 'to the centre of the box above finished floor level'. The floor tiles are not laid yet. How should you measure?
options: From the bare slab, ignoring the tiles
From the ceiling down to the box
From the planned finished floor, using the datum line
From the top edge of the skirting board, wherever it is

questions.stem: A contract says that work shall be 'to the satisfaction of the engineer'. Who decides whether the work is acceptable?
options: The electrician who did the work
The engineer named in the contract
The owner of the building next door
The power company's line crew

questions.stem: An LED fitting's datasheet gives '50 000 h L70'. What does this mean?
options: It uses 70 W for 50 000 hours
It has a 70% chance of lasting 50 000 hours
It needs cleaning every 50 000 hours
After 50 000 hours it still gives 70% of its first light

questions.stem: A lighting specification asks for lamps of 4000 K. What does 4000 K describe?
options: The colour of the light: a neutral white
The power the lamp uses
The lamp's expected life in hours
The brightness in lumens

questions.stem: A pump controller's manual has a commissioning checklist. Why should the team complete and sign it?
options: It shortens the warranty period
It takes the place of testing
It records that each set-up step was done
It is needed before spare parts can be ordered

questions.stem: You raise a query about an unclear item in a specification, and the designer answers. How should the answer be kept?
options: In your memory, to save paperwork
In writing, dated, and filed with the job records
Chalked on the wall beside the work
Only as a phone call to the foreman, to save time

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters ATS stand for, the switch that moves a load over to a standby generator by itself when the mains fails?
What do the letters SPD stand for, a device that protects equipment from voltage surges such as lightning?
What do the letters FLC stand for on a motor's data sheet?
What term is used for the largest fault current a breaker can safely interrupt, usually given in kA?
Which trip-curve letter is usually chosen for breakers on general lighting and socket circuits in homes?
What do the letters UPS stand for, a unit that keeps equipment running from batteries when the mains fails?
In what unit is the light output of a lamp given on its datasheet?
What do the letters CRI stand for on a lamp datasheet, a figure that shows how truly colours are seen under the light?
In the cable description 'XLPE/SWA/PVC', which material forms the outer sheath? Give its letters or name.
What rated residual operating current, in mA, is usual for an RCD that protects people against electric shock?
In an IP code, which letter is written in place of a digit when that kind of protection is not stated?
Terminal torque values are often given in N·m. What unit is N·m?
On a motor rating plate, what does the figure given in rev/min (rpm) tell you about the motor?
On a drawing, what does 'AFF' mean, as in 'socket 300 AFF'?
On a control schematic, what do the letters NC beside a contact mean?

essays.stem: You lead a team that will wire a new health clinic in Mandeville. You are given the specification, the drawings, the makers' datasheets and the national wiring code. Explain how you would review this pack before work starts, and what you would do with any problems you find.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first check that I have the latest revision of every document by comparing it with the drawing register, and remove any old copies. Then I read the specification in full, noting what it says about materials, cable types, workmanship, testing and handover. I compare the drawings with the specification, for example checking that the cable sizes, breaker ratings and fitting types agree. I check the makers' datasheets to see that the named equipment suits the clinic's supply (110/220 V, 50 Hz), the locations (IP ratings) and the loads. I check that nothing in the specification falls below the wiring code, since the code is the minimum. Where things disagree or are unclear, I write a dated query to the designer and wait for a written answer before that part is done. I keep a list of queries and answers. Finally, I brief the team on the key points and the answers, so everyone works to the same information.
markingPoints: Checks every document is the current revision
Reads the specification and compares it with the drawings
Checks equipment datasheets against supply, location and load
Checks nothing falls below the wiring code
Raises written queries, records answers and briefs the team

essays.stem: Explain how you would use a maker's datasheet to choose a circuit breaker for a 220 V circuit that feeds a 1.5 kW motor with a high starting current. Say what each figure you check means.
essays.modelAnswer: First I work out the running current: about 1500 ÷ (220 × power factor and efficiency) gives roughly 9–10 A, but I take the full-load current from the motor's rating plate. On the datasheet I check the rated current (In): it must be at or above the design current and not above the cable's rating, so a 16 A breaker may suit. I check the trip curve: a type B breaker trips instantly at 3–5 times In, which a motor's starting current may reach, so a type C (5–10 times In) is usually better for motors, as the designer approves. I check the breaking capacity in kA is at least the largest fault current at the board, so the breaker can clear a short circuit safely. I check the number of poles needed for 220 V and the rated voltage. Finally I check the terminal sizes and torque, and that the breaker fits the board. I record my choice and the reasons.
markingPoints: Uses the motor's full-load current as the design current
Rated current at or above design current and not above cable rating
Chooses the trip curve to allow for starting current (type C rather than B)
Breaking capacity at least the prospective fault current
Checks poles, voltage rating, terminals or torque, and records the choice

essays.stem: As team leader on a hotel rewiring job in Negril, describe how you would make sure everyone works from current drawings, and how changes made on site reach the as-built drawings.
essays.modelAnswer: I would keep a drawing register showing each drawing's number and latest revision. When a new revision arrives, I check the clouded changes, update the register, give the new copies to the team and collect the old ones, stamping them 'superseded' or destroying them so they cannot be used by mistake. At the morning briefing I tell the team what has changed. On site, I keep one set of drawings as the master mark-up set. When a change is agreed, for example a new cable route around a beam, I get the approval in writing, then mark the change in red on the master set, with the date and my initials. Team members tell me of any change so it is marked the same day. At the end of the job the mark-ups are used to produce the as-built drawings, which I check against the installation before they are handed to the client with the test results.
markingPoints: Keeps a drawing register with current revisions
Issues new revisions and withdraws or marks superseded copies
Briefs the team on what changed
Records approved site changes on a master mark-up set, dated and initialled
Turns mark-ups into checked as-built drawings for handover

essays.stem: A variable speed drive for a ventilation fan is to be installed. Explain how you would use its manual to install it safely, covering the supply, cabling, stored energy and setting it up.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the manual before starting, especially the safety and installation sections. I check the rating plate and manual agree with the supply voltage, frequency and the motor's power and current. I follow the mounting rules: the clearances for cooling, the temperature range and the IP rating for the room. For cabling, I use the cable types and sizes the manual gives, often screened motor cable, with the screen earthed as shown to reduce interference, and I keep motor cables away from control cables. I fit the protection the manual specifies. Before any work on it, I isolate, lock off and tag the supply, wait the discharge time given for the capacitors, and then prove dead with a tester checked before and after, including the DC bus. For setting up, I enter the motor data from the rating plate and the settings the manual lists, and record them. The first switch-on is done by an authorised person after the dead tests.
markingPoints: Checks supply and motor data against the manual and rating plate
Follows mounting, cooling and environment requirements
Uses specified cables, screening, earthing and separation from control cables
Safe isolation plus waiting for capacitor discharge and proving dead
Enters and records settings; first switch-on by an authorised person after tests

essays.stem: A specification lists the tests to be done on a new installation before it is energised and the forms on which to record them. Explain how you would plan and carry out these tests as a team, and what you would do if a result fails.
essays.modelAnswer: First I list each test the specification requires, such as continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance at the stated test voltage and polarity, and the forms to use. I check that our instruments are calibrated and in date, and that the team knows how to use them. The installation must be dead: I make sure the supply is not connected or is isolated, locked off and tagged, and proved dead with a tester checked before and after. Sensitive equipment, such as LED drivers and electronic controls, is disconnected before insulation tests so it is not damaged. Each circuit is tested in the order the forms set out, and each result is written down at once with the circuit number. Results are compared with the limits in the specification. If a result fails, the circuit is not energised; we find and repair the fault, retest, and record both results. I sign the forms and hand them to the person responsible for energising.
markingPoints: Lists the required tests and forms from the specification
Checks instruments are calibrated and the team can use them
Installation dead and safely isolated; sensitive equipment disconnected
Records each result at once and compares with the stated limits
Failed circuit not energised; fault fixed, retested and recorded

essays.stem: A client buys an air conditioner and a water pump abroad and asks you to install them. Explain what you would check in their manuals and rating plates before you agree, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I would check the supply voltage on each rating plate against what is available at the site: 110 V or 220 V. A 220 V unit cannot work on a 110 V circuit, and a 110 V unit would be damaged on 220 V. I would check that the rated frequency includes 50 Hz, because motors and compressors made only for a different frequency may run at the wrong speed and overheat here. I would check the current and power so that I can size the cable and the breaker, converting any imperial units in the manual, such as AWG wire sizes or horsepower, into metric with a reliable table and never rounding down a cable size. I would check the plug or connection type and any special protection the manual asks for. I would also check the installation rules, such as clearances and outdoor ratings. If anything does not suit, I explain it to the client in writing before work starts.
markingPoints: Checks voltage against 110 V or 220 V supply
Checks the frequency includes 50 Hz and explains why
Uses current and power to size cable and breaker
Converts imperial units correctly without rounding cable size down
Checks installation requirements and tells the client in writing if unsuitable

essays.stem: Your team will install a UPS with vented lead-acid batteries in a server room. Explain what you would look for in the battery safety data sheet and the UPS manual, and how you would use the information.
essays.modelAnswer: The safety data sheet tells me the hazards: the acid is corrosive to skin and eyes, and charging can give off hydrogen, which can explode. It gives the PPE: goggles or a face shield, acid-resistant gloves and an apron. It gives first aid: for acid in the eyes, rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes and get medical help. It also covers spills and storage. The UPS manual tells me the ventilation the battery area needs, the clearances, how to lift and connect the batteries, the order of connection and the torque for the terminals. I would use this to plan the job: arrange ventilation, have an eyewash station and a spill kit ready, ban flames and sparks, use insulated tools so a spanner cannot short the terminals, and wear the PPE. I would brief the team on the hazards and first aid before we start, and keep the documents on site.
markingPoints: Identifies corrosive acid and hydrogen gas hazards
Gives correct PPE from the SDS
Gives correct first aid for acid in the eyes (rinse at least 15 minutes, get help)
Uses the manual for ventilation, connection order, torque and handling
Plans controls: ventilation, eyewash, spill kit, no flames, insulated tools, team briefing

essays.stem: You must choose between two LED panel fittings for classrooms using their datasheets. Explain which figures you would compare and what each tells you.
essays.modelAnswer: I would compare the light output in lumens, to see which gives enough light for the classroom with fewer fittings. I would compare the power in watts and work out the efficacy in lumens per watt, since a higher figure means more light for less energy. I would look at the life rating, such as 50 000 h L70, which tells me how long until the light falls to 70% of its first value. I would check the colour temperature in kelvin, such as 4000 K for a neutral white suited to classrooms, and the colour rendering index (CRI), where a higher figure shows colours more truly. I would check the input voltage range covers our 110 V or 220 V supply and that the frequency includes 50 Hz, and check the power factor. I would check the IP rating, the size to fit the ceiling grid, and the warranty. I would then pick the one that best meets the specification for the lowest running cost.
markingPoints: Light output (lumens) and power (watts)
Efficacy in lumens per watt
Life rating (for example L70 hours)
Colour temperature and colour rendering
Supply voltage, frequency, power factor, IP rating or warranty checked

essays.stem: Explain the difference between a performance specification and a prescriptive specification. Give an electrical example of each, and say how you would show that your work meets each one.
essays.modelAnswer: A prescriptive specification tells you exactly what to use and how: for example, 'Lighting circuits shall be wired in 1.5 mm² cable in 20 mm PVC conduit, with a 10 A type B breaker.' To show I meet it, I use the named materials and methods, and the inspector can check them by looking and by checking the delivery notes. A performance specification tells you the result needed, but leaves the method to the installer or designer: for example, 'Each classroom shall have an average light level of at least 300 lux at desk height.' To show I meet it, I must prove the result, for example with a lighting calculation before the work, and a light meter reading at desk height after the work, recorded on a test sheet. Performance specifications give more choice but need proof by testing or calculation, while prescriptive ones are easier to check but give less freedom.
markingPoints: Defines prescriptive: states the materials and methods
Gives a correct electrical example of a prescriptive requirement
Defines performance: states the result needed
Gives a correct electrical example of a performance requirement
Explains how compliance is shown for each (inspection vs calculation and testing)

essays.stem: A client wants a standby generator connected to their house. Explain how you would use the maker's manual to install a manual changeover switch, and why the switch must never let the generator feed back into the power company's lines.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the changeover switch manual and the generator manual to check that their ratings suit the house load, the supply voltage and the generator output. The manual gives the mounting, the cable sizes, the terminal markings for the mains supply, the generator and the load, and the terminal torques. All work is done with the supply isolated: the main switch is off, locked and tagged, and the circuits are proved dead with a tester checked before and after. The power company's side of the meter is never touched. The changeover switch is wired so that the load can be connected to either the mains or the generator, but never both at the same time; its mechanical design prevents both being connected together. This matters because if the generator fed back into the lines, the transformer could raise its voltage to a dangerous level, and a lineworker repairing a line they believe is dead could be killed. The system is tested and inspected before use, and the client is shown how to use it.
markingPoints: Checks ratings in the manuals against load, voltage and generator
Follows the manual's mounting, cable, terminal and torque details
Works with the supply safely isolated and proved dead; never touches the power company's side
Explains break-before-make: load on mains or generator, never both
Explains that back-feed can kill lineworkers; system is tested and the client is shown how to use it

practical1.title: Review a specification pack and check delivered equipment against it
practical1.brief: As a group, review a small specification pack for a shop fit-out (specification pages, a layout drawing, a single-line diagram and makers' datasheets) and check a set of delivered items set out by the assessor against it. The items include breakers, an RCD, a cable off-cut with its markings, a light fitting and a small motor or its rating plate; some do not meet the specification. First, the group checks that each document is the current revision and lists any disagreements between them. Then each member takes at least one item: they read its rating plate or label, compare it with the specification and datasheet, record 'meets' or 'does not meet' on the group's compliance sheet with the reason, and photograph the label. Together, the group writes at least two dated queries to the designer about the problems found, and one member briefs the rest of the group on the findings while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Specification pack from the assessor: specification pages, layout drawing, single-line diagram and drawing register
Delivered items: breakers of different types and ratings, an RCD, a labelled cable off-cut, a light fitting, a motor or motor rating plate
Compliance check sheet and query (RFI) forms
Clipboards, highlighters and a red pen
photos: The documents laid out, with the revisions checked against the register
The rating plate or label of each item, close enough to read
Each member's entries on the compliance sheet
An item that does not meet the specification, with its label and the specification clause side by side
checklist: Checked the revisions against the drawing register and found any out-of-date document
Read the rating plate or label of their item correctly (voltage, frequency, current, curve, breaking capacity, IP or cable rating as it applies)
Compared the item with the specification and the datasheet and recorded a correct 'meets' or 'does not meet'
Gave a clear reason for each item that does not meet the specification
Took part in writing clear, dated queries to the designer
Took part in the briefing, or asked and answered questions during it
Handled the items carefully and returned them in their packaging
safety: No item is connected to any supply during this task
Handle breakers and fittings by their bodies; watch for sharp edges on cable ends and fitting frames
Lift the motor with help if it weighs more than you can lift safely, using the Centre's lifting rules

practical2.title: Set up starter components from makers' data on a dead training board, and write a work instruction
practical2.brief: As a group, use a motor's rating plate and the makers' datasheets for an overload relay, a timer relay and terminal blocks to set up a motor starter on a training board that is not connected to any supply. First, the board is shown to be isolated: the plug is removed or the isolator is locked and tagged, and one member proves it dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after, while the assessor watches. Then each member takes a part of the job: setting the overload relay to the full-load current from the rating plate, setting the timer relay to the time given in the job sheet, setting the torque screwdriver to the datasheet value (converting units if needed) and tightening the terminals, or checking another member's settings against the datasheets. Together, the group writes a one-page work instruction for this task, naming the manual sections used for each step. The assessor or the instructor carries out any function test on a protected bench; the group does not energise the board. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Training board with an overload relay, a timer relay, a contactor and terminal blocks, not connected to any supply
Motor, or motor rating plate, with a known full-load current
Makers' datasheets or manuals for the overload relay, timer relay and terminals
